clue.text: "The Monument" is a church — not a pub!

parts.note: CE is the usual abbreviation for the Church of England
taken as written
PH, short for public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a famous monument is really a church and certainly not a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'not' looks like a contradiction in the surface but simply supplies its own letters in the middle of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cenotaph in Whitehall is Britain's national war memorial, often referred to simply as the monument to the fallen.

clue.text: Lech Walesa's heart in pursuit of the Doge's

annotationWithheld.why: Lech Walesa's heart in pursuit of the Doge's (4): OGLE needs the middle of both Walesa (LE) and Doge (OG), so the single word 'heart' does two jobs, indicating both selections.
annotationWithheld.clue: Lech Walesa's heart in pursuit of the Doge's

clue.text: Health not right? Point to dairy product

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: 'Health!' and 'Cheers!' are both toasts said when raising a glass
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A worried question about one's health is followed by a pointer towards something from the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Health' here is the toast, not wellbeing: swapping it for its fellow toast and dropping an R leaves CHEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is made from curdled milk, a classic product of the dairy.

clue.text: See 25
Mature student works on one US academic subject

parts.note: OPS is short for opera, Latin for works
I is the Roman numeral one
Americans say math where Britons say maths

explanation.surface: A mature student is described as working on a single American college subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An opsimath is someone who begins to learn late in life, a rare word for a late learner.

clue.text: About adapting an endangered 17 animal

indicators.note: about can mean around or in a different order, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something about adapting a rare Chinese creature to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is the solution CHINESE, so the definition is an endangered Chinese animal. 'About' looks like 'concerning' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda, native to China's bamboo forests, has long been the emblem of endangered species.

clue.text: An inspiration in modern times, unlike Victoria

indicators.note: in places the source of inspiration inside the modern-era abbreviation

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks dates in the present era
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: A muse in the present day, in contrast to the stern Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously credited with the remark 'We are not amused', which the definition plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria was supposedly never entertained, so being tickled is the opposite of her reputed state.

clue.text: 17 recipe for happiness supplied with fungi she cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the ingredients are mixed up and transformed into something new

explanation.surface: A Chinese recipe for happiness made with mushrooms prepared by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is CHINESE. 'Recipe' and 'cooked' suggest a dish, but the recipe is for a harmonious home.
explanation.definitionFit: Feng shui is the Chinese art of arranging surroundings to bring harmony and good fortune.

clue.text: Optical equipment teacher returned in the afternoon

indicators.note: in places the turned-round teacher inside the afternoon abbreviation

parts.note: PM, post meridiem, means the afternoon

indicators.note: returned means the word for teacher is read backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A teacher comes back in the afternoon with some optical apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Optical equipment' is the definition; 'the afternoon' is the abbreviation that 'in' signals as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a glass block that bends and splits light, a standard piece of optics kit.

clue.text: Excavator of beauty spot

definitions.meaning: the small burrowing mammal digs tunnels underground
a small dark mark on the skin, sometimes called a beauty spot

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a burrowing animal that digs and a dark spot on the skin.

clue.text: It's seen running round tree by one on the spot

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters are placed around the tree
running suggests the letters are in motion and rearranged

parts.note: a yew is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: Something seen racing round a tree by a single person who happened to be there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like a verb about the person seen, but it is the anagram signal, and 'round' is a container signal rather than a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is a person who was present at the scene and saw events happen.

clue.text: Trade name

definitions.meaning: to deal in goods, as a dealer does stolen property
an informal word for a person's name or nickname

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to deal commercially in goods and, informally, what someone is called.

clue.text: Is wrong island in the river getting the wrong picture?

indicators.note: in places the three pieces inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Don is a river in Yorkshire, Scotland and Russia
taken as written
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A question whether an island in the river is mistaken, giving a false impression.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as someone getting the wrong idea, but 'wrong' is TORT, the legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: A distortion is a misrepresentation, an image or account bent out of its true shape.

clue.text: Mad rush to get stuffed in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places the word for stuffed inside the regional abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
tamped means packed down tightly, as tobacco in a pipe

explanation.surface: A frantic dash to get filled up in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, such as Surrey and Kent; here they stand for SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush, of cattle or of a crowd.

clue.text: Science produces happy ends thus in an afterthought

indicators.note: in puts the ends of happy and the word for thus inside the afterthought

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

indicators.note: ends means the first and last letters of happy

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A science produces a happy ending, as noted in a postscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy ends' means the outer letters of happy, not a happy ending; 'produces' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics is the natural science of matter, energy and motion.

clue.text: Study "Endeavour" and "Victory"

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a quest is a search or endeavour

explanation.surface: A study of two famous ships, Endeavour and Victory.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour and Victory are famous British ships, Cook's and Nelson's, which hides that they are ordinary words here.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a victory over an enemy, a territory won by force.

clue.text: Hastens to order rice menu with nasty consequences!

definitions.text: Hastens to order rice menu with nasty consequences!

indicators.note: to order means to arrange, so the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to order from a rice menu and pays an unpleasant price afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' sounds like ordering food but signals the anagram; the leftover 'with' and 'consequences' complete the picture of the after-effects of a takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the headaches and flushing once blamed on monosodium glutamate in takeaway food from China.

clue.text: See 17
Don't pay expert to secure gold plate

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the expert word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: deft means skilful or expert
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
an L-plate is the learner's plate on a UK car, so plate gives L

explanation.surface: Someone who skips payment hires an expert to secure some gold plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold plate' looks like one item but splits into AU and L; in Britain learner drivers display a red L on a white plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To default is to fail to make a payment that is due on a loan or debt.

clue.text: Peacemakers interrupting heartless miser with appeal for funds

indicators.note: interrupting means the peacemakers break into the middle of the miser
heartless means the central letter of the miser's name is dropped

parts.note: Scrooge is the miser in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
the UN, United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: Peace envoys break in on a cold-hearted miser to ask for donations.
explanation.walkthrough: The miser is Dickens's Ebenezer; 'heartless' drops his central letter and 'interrupting' breaks the remainder open for the peacemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to cadge or beg for money or goods from others.

clue.text: 24 across, or large-bottomed?

definitions.meaning: 24 across is the clue for impudent, so this sense is saucy or impudent
humorously, having big cheeks, that is buttocks

explanation.definitionFit: The word means impudent, and jokingly suggests someone with sizeable buttock cheeks.

clue.text: Get thee hence (relative to a 5)

indicators.note: to here means the relative is attached after the other pieces

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: An archaic dismissal with a parenthetical note about a relative and a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 here is not the clue 5 but the Roman numeral V.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaunt is an archaic command meaning go away, the same as begone.

clue.text: Mounted musical, keeping chorus leader busy

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the musical surrounds the leader
in a down clue mounted means the musical is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of chorus

explanation.surface: A musical is staged and keeps its chorus leader busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' sounds like staging a show, but in a down clue it turns EVITA upwards to ATIVE; C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Active means busy, occupied and engaged in doing things.

clue.text: See 17
Impudent every time

parts.note: per means for each, as in once per day

explanation.surface: Someone who is cheeky on every single occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pert describes a person who is saucily bold or forward in manner.

clue.text: Succeed with a saucy suggestion

definitions.meaning: to get through an examination or test successfully
an amorous advance, as in making one at someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to succeed in a test, and an amorous approach made to someone.

clue.text: Desperately seeks aid to keep 17 23 utensils from 17 23 18

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the jumbled letters surround the utensils
desperately suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 17 23 is CHINESE RESTAURANT, and woks are the pans used in its kitchens

explanation.surface: Someone frantically seeks help to keep pans from a Chinese restaurant, having been made ill by its food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperately' signals the anagram and 'to keep' the container. The definition refers to the linked answer 17 23 18; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition was first described by Dr Robert Ho Man Kwok in 1968, and his name became an alternative label for it.

clue.text: To be that fond of the compiler is charming

parts.note: to be fond of someone is to love them
so means that much, as in so fond
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The setter suggests that being so fond of them would be delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read 'love so me' in order; the compiler is the crossword setter speaking of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovesome is an old word meaning lovely or attractive, charming to look at.
